segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome back to EnglishPod.

segments.zh: 我叫凯瑟琳，今天我们为大家准备了一节关于金钱的中高级课程。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: We are going to talk about the stock market.
segments.zh: 我们将讨论股市。

segments.en: So a very interesting topic, very current as well because well throughout the world stock markets are not doing very well.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个非常有趣、也非常当下的话题，因为世界各地的股票市场表现都不太好。

segments.en: That's right and you may have seen on the television a lot of information about this.
segments.zh: 没错，你可能在电视上看到了很多关于这方面的信息。

segments.en: So today we're going to hopefully explain some of the things and phrases and words that you've been hearing.
segments.zh: 所以今天我们将有望解释一些你一直听到的东西、短语和单词。

segments.en: But first we've got a couple of important indicators, a couple of acronyms actually that you're going to hear about.
segments.zh: 但首先我们有几个重要的指标，实际上是你会听到的几个首字母缩略词。

segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So the first word that we have on vocabulary preview is the NASDAQ.
segments.zh: 所以我们在词汇预览中的第一个词是纳斯达克。

segments.en: NASDAQ.
segments.zh: 纳斯达克。

segments.en: NASDAQ.
segments.zh: 纳斯达克。

segments.en: N-A-S-D-A-Q.
segments.zh: 拼写是 N-A-S-D-A-Q。

segments.en: So this is basically the American stock market.
segments.zh: 所以这基本上是美国股市。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: It's an acronym.
segments.zh: 这是个首字母缩略词。

segments.en: Now it's a really, really long acronym so we're not going to get into it but it is basically the American stock market where all these companies are trading stock, publicly traded companies.
segments.zh: 它是一个非常非常长的首字母缩略词，所以我们就不细说了，但它基本上就是美国股市，所有这些公司都在这里交易股票，也就是上市公司。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So publicly traded companies, you're basically trading their stocks through NASDAQ.
segments.zh: 所以上市公司，你基本上是通过纳斯达克交易他们的股票。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And now the next one that we have is an indicator which tells us how well some companies or some stock are doing and that's the Dow Jones indicator.
segments.zh: 接下来我们要讲的是一个指标，它能告诉我们某些公司或某些股票的表现如何，那就是道琼斯指数。

segments.en: Dow Jones indicator.
segments.zh: 道琼斯指标。

segments.en: So maybe if the Dow Jones is really low for something, we think, man, it's not doing so well.
segments.zh: 所以如果道琼斯指数真的很低，我们就会想，天哪，情况不太好。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: If it goes up, things are improving.
segments.zh: 如果上涨，情况正在好转。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So usually the Dow Jones has the, it's based upon the 50 biggest companies in the United States, the 50 biggest publicly traded companies.
segments.zh: 因此，道琼斯通常有，它基于美国 50 家最大的公司，即 50 家最大的上市公司。

segments.en: Now you can divide it into like industrial companies or pharmaceutical companies, etc.
segments.zh: 现在你可以把它分成工业公司或制药公司等。

segments.en: But in general, that's the indicator and how it works.
segments.zh: 但总的来说，这就是指标以及它的工作方式。

segments.en: Great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: So we're going to listen to today's dialogue and find out how these words are used in context and we're back in a moment to talk about what's going on.
segments.zh: 所以我们要听今天的对话，找出这些词是如何在上下文中使用的，我们很快就会回来谈论正在发生的事情。

segments.en: Sorry to bother you, sir, but I have some bad news.
segments.zh: 很抱歉打扰您，先生，但我有一些坏消息。

segments.en: What is it?
segments.zh: 怎么了？

segments.en: Well, the stock market just took a huge plunge and we've lost a lot of money.
segments.zh: 好吧，股市刚刚大跌，我们损失了很多钱。

segments.en: What do you mean?
segments.zh: 你是什么意思？

segments.en: What happened?
segments.zh: 发生什么事了？

segments.en: There are many factors that weigh in, but NASDAQ is down 200 points.
segments.zh: 影响因素很多，但纳斯达克下降了200点。

segments.en: The Dow Jones indicator also suffered.
segments.zh: 道琼斯指数也遭受了损失。

segments.en: Our portfolio is worth half of what it was worth one week ago.
segments.zh: 我们的投资组合价值是一周前的价值的一半。

segments.en: How is this possible?
segments.zh: 这怎么可能？

segments.en: You are supposed to be talking to our stockbrokers and making sure that our securities and investments are safe and making a profitable return.
segments.zh: 您应该与我们的股票经纪人交谈，并确保我们的证券和投资是安全的并获得有利可图的回报。

segments.en: I know, sir.
segments.zh: 我知道，先生。

segments.en: We didn't expect a bull market to become a bear market all of a sudden.
segments.zh: 我们没想到牛市会突然变成熊市。

segments.en: On the other hand, you still have some high yield trash bonds and government bonds that will give us enough liquidity to cut our losses and reinvest in emerging markets.
segments.zh: 另一方面，你仍然有一些高收益的垃圾债券和政府债券，这将为我们提供足够的流动性来减少我们的损失并在新兴市场进行再投资。

segments.en: We could potentially make this tragedy work for us and make us think outside the box.
segments.zh: 我们或许能把这场危机转化为机会，也借此跳出常规思路。

segments.en: Do what you have to do.
segments.zh: 做你必须做的事。

segments.en: One other thing.
segments.zh: 另一件事。

segments.en: Don't tell the rest of the stockholders about this.
segments.zh: 不要告诉其他股东这件事。

segments.en: If they find out it's the end of this company.
segments.zh: 如果他们发现了，这家公司就完了。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So a lot of interesting words there.
segments.zh: 这里有不少有意思的词。

segments.en: I think a lot of them were very specific to the stock market and very, maybe a little bit difficult.
segments.zh: 我觉得其中很多词都和股市密切相关，而且可能有点难。

segments.zh: 我们为什么不看其中几个，进入语言要点。

segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Okay, so this first word is a very important word in banking and finance.
segments.zh: 好的，所以第一个词是银行和金融中非常重要的词。

segments.en: We talk about portfolios a lot.
segments.zh: 我们经常谈论投资组合。

segments.en: So portfolio.
segments.zh: 所以投资组合。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So basically a portfolio is the variety of things that you own.
segments.zh: 所以基本上一个投资组合是你拥有的各种东西。

segments.en: For example, in the stock market, it could be stocks, it could be bonds, it can be mutual funds, etc.
segments.zh: 例如，在股票市场上，它可以是股票，可以是债券，可以是共同基金等。

segments.en: Or for example, if you're a company, your product portfolio could be all the products that your company owns.
segments.zh: 或者，例如，如果您是一家公司，您的产品组合可能是您公司拥有的所有产品。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So in this case, our portfolio is worth half what it was a week ago.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，我们的投资组合价值是一周前的一半。

segments.en: And so this is a sentence that means, we've lost half of the money we invested.
segments.zh: 所以这个句子意思是，我们损失了一半的投资。

segments.en: All of our investments are in a portfolio.
segments.zh: 我们所有的投资都在一个投资组合中。

segments.en: We talk about them as a portfolio.
segments.zh: 我们将它们视为投资组合。

segments.en: And when we lose money, we say our portfolio is worth less now than it was before.
segments.zh: 当我们赔钱时，我们说我们的投资组合现在的价值低于以前。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So moving on, he starts to talk about the bull market and the bear market.
segments.zh: 接下来，他开始谈论牛市和熊市。

segments.en: So what is this all about?
segments.zh: 那么这是怎么回事呢？

segments.en: Well, a bull is an animal with horns.
segments.zh: 嗯，公牛是有角的动物。

segments.en: And a bear is another animal.
segments.zh: 熊是另一种动物。

segments.en: So we're not talking about animals here.
segments.zh: 所以我们在这里不是在谈论动物。

segments.en: We're talking about special finance phrases.
segments.zh: 我们谈论的是特殊的财务短语。

segments.en: So the bull market would be, again, talking about companies and trading.
segments.zh: 因此，牛市将再次谈论公司和交易。

segments.en: It would be maybe a market that's growing very rapidly.
segments.zh: 这可能是一个快速增长的市场。

segments.en: That's very, very strong.
segments.zh: 这是非常非常强大的。

segments.en: That's a bull market.
segments.zh: 那是牛市。

segments.en: So people often talk about China's bull market, right?
segments.zh: 所以人们经常谈论中国的牛市，对吧？

segments.en: How China continues to grow and grow and grow and grow.
segments.zh: 中国如何继续成长、成长、成长和成长。

segments.en: But a market that slows down, like the United States last year, would be a bear market.
segments.zh: 但像去年美国一样放缓的市场将是熊市。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So think of a bear, maybe it's sleeping, it goes into hibernation.
segments.zh: 所以想想一只熊，也许它在睡觉，它进入冬眠状态。

segments.en: That's a bear market.
segments.zh: 那是熊市。

segments.en: So a slow market.
segments.zh: 所以就是一个低迷的市场。

segments.en: It's not really growing.
segments.zh: 它并没有真正增长。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: But talking about a portfolio again, we might have stocks.
segments.zh: 但再谈到投资组合，我们可能有股票。

segments.en: But in this case, the two people are talking about their bonds.
segments.zh: 但在这种情况下，两人正在谈论他们的债券。

segments.en: So he says, you still have some high yield trash bonds and government bonds.
segments.zh: 所以他说，你仍然有一些高收益的垃圾债券和政府债券。

segments.en: What's a high yield bond and what's a trash bond?
segments.zh: 什么是高收益债券，什么是垃圾债券？

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So when we think about the word yield is how much it gives, right?
segments.zh: 所以当我们想到 yield 是它给了多少，对吧？

segments.en: So how much we are getting from it.
segments.zh: 那么我们从中得到了多少。

segments.en: So something that is high yield means that you're getting a lot from it.
segments.zh: 所以高产的东西意味着你从中得到了很多。

segments.en: For example, this orange tree yields 300 oranges per year.
segments.zh: 例如，这棵橙树每年可产生 300 个橙子。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So how much we get from it.
segments.zh: 那么我们从中得到了多少。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So we're getting 300 oranges.
segments.zh: 所以我们得到了300个橙子。

segments.en: That's how much it's yielding.
segments.zh: 这就是它的产量。

segments.en: And so basically that's what yield means.
segments.zh: 所以基本上这就是收益率的含义。

segments.en: So when we talk about trash bonds, this on the other hand, it's a word that's maybe a little bit tricky, but a bond is a promise that you get from the seller that he's going to pay you back the money that you give him with interest.
segments.zh: 所以当我们谈论垃圾债券时，另一方面，这是一个可能有点棘手的词，但债券是卖方给你的一个承诺，他会连本带息把你给他的钱还给你。

segments.en: But a trash bond is a very risky bond.
segments.zh: 但垃圾债券是一种非常危险的债券。

segments.en: It means that the seller might not pay you back because he's still trying to get all the money.
segments.zh: 这意味着卖家可能不会偿还您，因为他仍在努力获得所有的钱。

segments.en: Right, but a high yield trash bond means that you might make a lot of money from this bond unless of course it's not very dependable.
segments.zh: 是的，但高收益的垃圾债券意味着你可能会从这种债券中赚很多钱，除非它当然不是很可靠。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So it's risky.
segments.zh: 所以有风险。

segments.en: Of course, since it's riskier, it has more yield.
segments.zh: 当然，由于它的风险更大，它的收益率更高。

segments.en: Great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: So high yields trash bond.
segments.zh: 那么，高收益垃圾债券。

segments.en: And then what about this?
segments.zh: 那么这个呢？

segments.en: They will give us liquidity to cut our losses.
segments.zh: 他们将给我们流动性来减少我们的损失。

segments.en: Liquidity.
segments.zh: 流动性。

segments.en: We hear all about liquidity in finance.
segments.zh: 我们听到了有关金融流动性的所有信息。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Maybe in your company, the accountant will talk about this.
segments.zh: 也许在你的公司，会计师会谈论这个。

segments.en: And that's basically just to have money cash in hand.
segments.zh: 这基本上就是指手头有现金。

segments.en: So you have money to pay things or to buy things.
segments.zh: 所以你有钱来付账或买东西。

segments.en: Not with...
segments.zh: 不是用……

segments.en: So it's available.
segments.zh: 所以它是可用的。

segments.en: Available, yeah.
segments.zh: 可用，是的。

segments.en: Not with credit.
segments.zh: 不是靠赊账。

segments.en: The opposite of credit.
segments.zh: 信用的反面。

segments.en: Okay, liquidity.
segments.zh: 好吧，流动性。

segments.en: And finally, instead, what are we going to do?
segments.zh: 最后，相反，我们要做什么？

segments.en: Let's think outside the box.
segments.zh: 让我们跳出框框思考。

segments.en: We could reinvest in emerging markets.
segments.zh: 我们可以对新兴市场进行再投资。

segments.en: And this is a very hot topic lately, talking about emerging markets.
segments.zh: 这是最近一个非常热门的话题，谈论新兴市场。

segments.en: So to emerge means to come up, to rise.
segments.zh: 所以 emerge 的意思是兴起、上升。

segments.en: Yeah, to come out.
segments.zh: 是的，要出来。

segments.en: So it's almost like new or growing markets.
segments.zh: 所以它几乎就像新的或不断增长的市场。

segments.en: So in this case, a market, an emerging market would be, for example, the Southeast Asian market, which is growing quickly, or even you could say West African market.
segments.zh: 因此，在这种情况下，一个市场，一个新兴市场将是，例如，正在快速增长的东南亚市场，甚至可以说是西非市场。

segments.en: We're talking about places in the world that aren't established.
segments.zh: 我们说的是世界上那些尚未发展成熟的地区。

segments.en: They're not old and dependable.
segments.zh: 它们并不古老，也谈不上可靠。

segments.en: They're new and exciting.
segments.zh: 它们是新兴的、令人兴奋的。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So they're coming up.
segments.zh: 所以它们正在崛起。

segments.en: So that's an emerging market.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个新兴市场。

segments.en: So a lot of very interesting words and phrases.
segments.zh: 所以很多非常有趣的单词和短语。

segments.en: They're very related to our topic.
segments.zh: 它们与我们的主题非常相关。

segments.en: And so why don't we move on now.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不现在继续前进。

segments.en: Let's take a look at two key phrases on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 让我们来看看关于流利表达的两个关键短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: This first phrase is something we've heard a lot about in the last year or two with things not going so well in the world of finance.
segments.zh: 第一个短语是我们在过去一两年里经常听到的，因为金融界的情况不太好。

segments.en: The first one, here we go, to cut our losses.
segments.zh: 第一个，我们开始，减少我们的损失。

segments.en: Okay, so let's cut our losses.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们减少损失。

segments.en: So when you talk about cutting your losses, that means to try and stop losing money somehow, maybe sell early.
segments.zh: 因此，当您谈论减少损失时，这意味着尝试以某种方式停止亏损，也许提前出售。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So in this case, we're losing money.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，我们正在亏损。

segments.en: Let's stop now.
segments.zh: 让我们现在停下来。

segments.en: Let's stop everything.
segments.zh: 让我们停止一切。

segments.en: Cut our losses.
segments.zh: 减少我们的损失。

segments.en: That means cut them away.
segments.zh: 意思就是割舍掉它们。

segments.en: Forget about them.
segments.zh: 忘记他们。

segments.en: Throw them away and start again.
segments.zh: 把它们扔掉，重新开始。

segments.en: Okay, so we could say, my business is failing.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们可以说，我的生意正在失败。

segments.en: I'm going to cut my losses, sell the business and start again.
segments.zh: 我将减少损失，出售业务并重新开始。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: That's exactly it.
segments.zh: 正是如此。

segments.en: So to cut your losses means to stop doing something, maybe sell it and stop losing money.
segments.zh: 所以减少损失意味着停止做某事，也许卖掉它并停止亏损。

segments.en: Basically, you accept the fact that you lost it.
segments.zh: 基本上，你接受你失去它的事实。

segments.en: You can't get it back and start again.
segments.zh: 你不能把它拿回来，重新开始。

segments.en: So when they were talking about investing in emerging markets, he said, well, maybe we could do this and that would force us to think outside the box.
segments.zh: 因此，当他们谈论投资新兴市场时，他说，好吧，也许我们可以这样做，这将迫使我们跳出框框思考。

segments.en: Okay, this is a great phrase and you might hear this in meetings a lot or from your manager.
segments.zh: 好的，这是一个很棒的短语，你可能经常在会议上或从经理那里听到。

segments.en: What's going on here is these two people are talking about how they lost a lot of money.
segments.zh: 这里发生的事情是这两个人在谈论他们是如何损失很多钱的。

segments.en: The economy is bad and they've been doing things in a normal way for a long time.
segments.zh: 经济很糟糕，他们一直以正常的方式做事很长一段时间。

segments.en: It's not working.
segments.zh: 它不工作。

segments.en: Let's think outside the box.
segments.zh: 让我们跳出框框思考。

segments.en: That means let's be creative.
segments.zh: 这意味着让我们发挥创造力。

segments.en: Let's try and discover new ways of doing things that will yield positive results.
segments.zh: 让我们尝试发现会产生积极结果的新方法。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: This is a very, very common phrase, very widely used in business or when you're talking about ideas is people tell you to think outside the box to maybe break some of the rules.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常非常常见的短语，在商业中非常广泛地使用，或者当你在谈论想法时，人们告诉你要跳出框框思考可能会打破一些规则。

segments.en: Right, right.
segments.zh: 对，对。

segments.en: Don't just think the way that you always do.
segments.zh: 不要总是按你一贯的方式思考。

segments.en: Don't do the same thing over and over.
segments.zh: 不要一遍又一遍地做同样的事情。

segments.en: Do something new, be creative, come up with something great.
segments.zh: 做一些新的事情，要有创意，想出一些伟大的东西。

segments.en: So that's thinking outside the box.
segments.zh: 所以这就是跳出框框思考。

segments.en: Right, very good.
segments.zh: 对，很好。

segments.en: So a lot of great phrases there.
segments.zh: 所以那里有很多很棒的短语。

segments.en: I think we've learned quite a bit.
segments.zh: 我想我们学到了很多。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to the dialogue one last time and we'll be back to talk a little bit more about this very interesting topic.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不上次听对话，我们会回来多谈谈这个非常有趣的话题。

segments.en: Sorry to bother you, sir, but I have some bad news.
segments.zh: 很抱歉打扰您，先生，但我有一些坏消息。

segments.en: What is it?
segments.zh: 怎么了？

segments.en: Well, the stock market just took a huge plunge and we've lost a lot of money.
segments.zh: 好吧，股市刚刚大跌，我们损失了很多钱。

segments.en: What do you mean?
segments.zh: 你是什么意思？

segments.en: What happened?
segments.zh: 发生什么事了？

segments.en: There are many factors that weigh in, but Nasdaq is down 200 points.
segments.zh: 影响因素很多，但纳斯达克下降了200点。

segments.en: The Dow Jones indicator also suffered.
segments.zh: 道琼斯指数也遭受了损失。

segments.en: Our portfolio is worth half of what it was worth one week ago.
segments.zh: 我们的投资组合价值是一周前的价值的一半。

segments.en: How is this possible?
segments.zh: 这怎么可能？

segments.en: You are supposed to be talking to our stockbrokers and making sure that our securities and investments are safe and making a profitable return.
segments.zh: 您应该与我们的股票经纪人交谈，并确保我们的证券和投资是安全的并获得有利可图的回报。

segments.en: I know, sir.
segments.zh: 我知道，先生。

segments.en: We didn't expect a bull market to become a bear market all of a sudden.
segments.zh: 我们没想到牛市会突然变成熊市。

segments.en: On the other hand, you still have some high yield trash bonds and government bonds that will give us enough liquidity to cut our losses and reinvest in emerging markets.
segments.zh: 另一方面，你仍然有一些高收益的垃圾债券和政府债券，这将为我们提供足够的流动性来减少我们的损失并在新兴市场进行再投资。

segments.en: We could potentially make this tragedy work for us and make us think outside the box.
segments.zh: 我们或许能把这场危机转化为机会，也借此跳出常规思路。

segments.en: Do what you have to do.
segments.zh: 做你必须做的事。

segments.en: One other thing.
segments.zh: 另一件事。

segments.en: Don't tell the rest of the stockholders about this.
segments.zh: 不要告诉其他股东这件事。

segments.en: If they find out it's the end of this company.
segments.zh: 如果他们发现了，这家公司就完了。

segments.en: So I remember being a little kid and watching TV with my parents and on the news there was always the business segment and in this you'd always hear the Nasdaq is down 10 points.
segments.zh: 所以我记得小时候和父母一起看电视，新闻里总是有财经板块，在里面你总能听到纳斯达克下跌了 10 点。

segments.en: The Dow Jones Industrial today is down 10 points.
segments.zh: 道琼斯工业指数今天下跌了 10 点。

segments.en: Yesterday was up two.
segments.zh: 昨天上涨了两点。

segments.en: That's an average of H. Okay.
segments.zh: 这是 H 的平均值。好吧。

segments.en: Yeah, it's very complicated, especially if you take a look also in the newspaper.
segments.zh: 是的，这很复杂，特别是如果你也看报纸。

segments.en: Sometimes it shows you different publicly traded companies and it has a bunch of numbers.
segments.zh: 有时它会向您展示不同的上市公司，并且有很多数字。

segments.en: It's a very interesting topic.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的话题。

segments.en: It's almost a science, I think.
segments.zh: 我想这几乎是一门科学。

segments.en: Very much a science and some people have made a lot of money playing the stock market and trying to buy stocks when they're low, wait until they're high, sell them off and make tons.
segments.zh: 一门科学，有些人在股票市场上赚了很多钱，并试图在股票低的时候买入股票，等到它们高点，卖掉它们，赚很多钱。

segments.en: Yeah, it's pretty much analyzing risk.
segments.zh: 是的，这几乎是在分析风险。

segments.en: So making calculated decisions and that's why they use all these formulas and all these different ratios and ways to ponder how much they should invest or what would they gain.
segments.zh: 因此，做出有计划的决定，这就是为什么他们使用所有这些公式以及所有这些不同的比率和方式来思考他们应该投资多少或他们会获得什么。

segments.en: So it's very, very interesting.
segments.zh: 所以它非常非常有趣。

segments.en: Many people compare it to gambling, but it's kind of like gambling but not really because you don't really depend on luck.
segments.zh: 许多人将其与赌博进行比较，但这有点像赌博，但不是真的，因为您并不真正依赖运气。

segments.en: You kind of make calculated decisions.
segments.zh: 你做出有计划的决定。

segments.en: And sometimes you're trading for big, big companies or even parts of big markets like parts of entire countries.
segments.zh: 有时你会为大公司，甚至是整个国家的大市场的一部分进行交易。

segments.en: A lot of people, for example, stockbrokers will invest a group of workers' retirement funds.
segments.zh: 例如，很多人会投资一组工人的退休基金。

segments.en: They will take those funds and be like, hey, you're maybe getting 5% from the bank for keeping your money there.
segments.zh: 他们会拿走这些资金，就像，嘿，你可能会从银行那里得到 5% 的钱来把你的钱存在那里。

segments.en: Give me the money and I'll give you 25% yield on your investment.
segments.zh: 给我钱，我会给你 25% 的投资收益。

segments.en: And so obviously they're playing not only their reputation but also with other people's life savings.
segments.zh: 显然，他们赌上的不仅是自己的声誉，还有别人的毕生积蓄。

segments.en: And that's why a lot of people lost money when two years ago the bubble really burst in a lot of areas like real estate.
segments.zh: 这就是为什么很多人在两年前像房地产这样的许多领域的泡沫真正破裂时赔钱的原因。

segments.en: Stock prices went down.
segments.zh: 股价下跌。

segments.en: The United States went into a recession.
segments.zh: 美国陷入了衰退。

segments.en: And all these people's retirement funds, their savings, they lost it.
segments.zh: 而这些人所有的退休基金、他们的储蓄，全都赔了进去。

segments.en: So you got to be careful with this kind of stuff and do your homework.
segments.zh: 所以对这种事情你得多加小心，做好功课。

segments.en: But that's about it for us today.
segments.zh: 但这对我们今天来说就是这样。

segments.en: Hope that you've enjoyed this lesson.
segments.zh: 希望你喜欢这节课。

segments.zh: 如果您有任何问题或意见，请访问我们的网站 englishpod.com。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: We'll see everyone there.
segments.zh: 到时候见，各位。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
